transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello... well... I suppose it's because of some things at church. I guess I've been doing odd things lately. Like... at the potluck table, I'll just stand there holding the serving spoon up in the air. Just not moving. Or... I'll sit and fold the same stack of napkins over and over again, while folks are just standing there waiting on me. I'm not really sure why.

When you're holding the spoon in the air or folding the napkins, do you feel like you're doing it on purpose but can't stop, or does it feel like your body is just doing it without you controlling it?
I... I don't rightly know. I haven't really thought on it like that. I just... I guess I'm just doing it. It's hard to say.

When you're doing these things—holding the spoon or folding the napkins—do you hear voices telling you to do them, or do you have thoughts in your head about needing to do them? Or does it feel more like your body just moves on its own without any thoughts behind it?
No... no voices. I don't hear anything like that. Just... my own thoughts, I suppose. It's just... quiet. I don't know why I do it. I just... do.
When you're standing there holding the spoon up in the air, if someone gently tried to move your arm down, would your arm move easily, or would it feel stiff and resist the movement?
I... well, I couldn't rightly say. Nobody's ever tried to pull my arm down or anything when I get like that. They mostly just stand there looking at me. So I don't know.
Have you noticed any changes in how your muscles feel—like stiffness or tension—when you're doing these things, or do your muscles feel normal?
I don't... I don't really notice anything like that. Just... normal, I guess. I haven't paid it much mind.
Do you feel like something is wrong with you, or do you think everything is fine and normal?
I don't... I don't really know. I suppose... maybe things are a bit different. But I don't feel like anything's terribly wrong. Just... getting older, maybe. I don't really think about it much.
If I gently moved your arm into a position while you're having one of these episodes, do you think your arm would stay in that position, or would it go back to where it was before?
I... I can't really say. Like I mentioned, nobody's ever touched me or tried to move me when it happens. So... I don't know what it would do.
When you're standing there holding the spoon in the air, do you stay in that exact position for a long time, or do you eventually move and go back to doing normal things?
I... I'm not really sure. I don't keep track of the time. I guess I just... eventually put it down and go back to what I was doing. It's hard to say.

When you're doing these things like holding the spoon or folding the napkins, if someone were to gently move your arm or hand into a different position, do you think your arm would stay where they put it, or do you think you'd move it back?
I... we just talked about this. I haven't had anyone try to move me. So I couldn't tell you.
When you're holding the spoon in the air like that, if I were to gently guide your arm down, would your arm feel like it's resisting me, or would it move down fairly easily?
I don't... I don't know. Like I said, nobody has tried. So I really couldn't tell you how it would feel.
During one of these episodes, if I were to slowly and gently move your arm up above your head while you're standing there, and then let go, would your arm stay up there, or would it fall back down?
I... I really don't know. You keep asking me about people moving my arm, but... like I said, nobody's ever done it. So I just... I don't know what it would do.

I'd like to do a brief physical examination if that's okay with you. I'm going to gently lift your arm up and hold it there for a moment. Just relax and let me do this—don't try to help me or resist. Is that alright?
...I guess so. If you need to.

I'm going to gently lift your arm up and hold it in the air above your head, and then I'm going to let go. When I let go, does your arm stay up there in the air, or does it fall back down to your side?
...It stayed up. I didn't mean to keep it there, it just... stayed.

Besides these episodes at church with the spoon and napkins, have you noticed anything strange happening in your thinking or beliefs lately? For example, do you feel like people are watching you, or do you have any unusual thoughts that seem very real to you?
...No. I haven't noticed anything like that. Nobody is watching me. I just... I mind my own business mostly. So, no.

Over the past few weeks or months, have you had any beliefs that you felt very strongly about—things that seemed absolutely true to you—even if other people didn't agree or didn't understand why you believed them?
...No. I don't think so. I just... I just have my normal thoughts. Nothing that other people would disagree with, I don't think.

When did you first start noticing these episodes with the spoon and napkins at church? Was it something that started suddenly over days or weeks, or has it been happening gradually over months or longer?

...I don't know exactly. It's just... maybe around six months ago. That's when people started saying I was acting strange... and talking weird. I didn't think it was that sudden. Just... about six months, I guess.
Over these past six months, have you noticed any shaking or trembling in your hands or arms, or any other parts of your body that move on their own without you trying to make them move?
...No. I haven't noticed anything shaking. Just... my hands are fine. I don't shake.

During these episodes when you're holding the spoon or folding the napkins, are you aware of what's happening around you—like can you hear people talking or see them looking at you—or does it feel like you're in your own world?
...I don't know. I guess... I hear them. I'm not... I'm not somewhere else. I just... I'm just sitting there.
Outside of these episodes at church, do you talk and interact normally with people, or have you noticed that you're speaking less or responding less to people around you in general?
...I guess I talk less. I don't really... interact much. Just keep to myself mostly.

G25.82 (tardive dyskinesia) is ruled out as there is no history of antipsychotic use mentioned and the presentation is more consistent with primary psychiatric catatonia rather than medication-induced movement disorder.

opening_question.question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with waxy flexibility (arm remaining elevated when passively positioned), psychomotor immobility (prolonged holding of spoon, repetitive napkin folding), reduced speech and social withdrawal, and gradual onset over approximately 6 months. These findings are consistent with catatonia associated with schizophrenia spectrum disorder. While conversion disorder (F44.5) was considered due to the apparent motor symptoms, the constellation of symptoms—including waxy flexibility on examination, social withdrawal, speech reduction, and insidious onset—better aligns with catatonic schizophrenia. The absence of clear psychotic symptoms (delusions, hallucinations) does not exclude schizophrenia, as catatonic presentations may predominate.
